title: Pipe and Plate Templates
objective: Recognise how pipe and plate template information represents required shapes and features, and why controlled job information must remain the authority.
safety_boundary: Learning only. This lesson develops recognition and understanding. It does not authorise practical marking-out, cutting, heating, forming, welding, machine operation or fabrication.

sections.heading: Why are pipe and plate templates used?
sections.body: Pipe and plate work can involve shapes, openings, profiles and relationships that must correspond with approved job information. A template can provide a controlled representation of the required feature.

sections.heading: Pipe template information
sections.body: Pipe-related templates can represent required profiles or relationships associated with a particular component or joint. The template must correspond to the correct pipe or component, orientation and controlled job reference.

sections.heading: Plate template information
sections.body: Plate-related templates can represent outlines, profiles, openings or repeated features specified by controlled job information.

sections.heading: Identity, orientation and revision
sections.body: Before relying on template information, recognise the importance of checking identity, intended component or feature, orientation and current revision or issue status.

sections.heading: Relationship to drawings and specifications
sections.body: Templates do not stand alone. They must remain connected to the approved information that defines the job.

sections.heading: Recognition before practical work
sections.body: At knowledge level, recognise what a pipe or plate template represents, how it is identified, and why its controlled source matters.

questions.question: What remains the authority when a pipe or plate template is used?
options: The current approved drawing, specification or job information
questions.answer: The current approved drawing, specification or job information

questions.question: Why must a template be correctly identified?
options: To confirm that it relates to the intended job, component or feature
Because similar-looking templates are always interchangeable
questions.answer: To confirm that it relates to the intended job, component or feature

questions.question: What should you do when template identity, orientation or revision is unclear?
options: Choose what looks closest and continue
Stop and clarify through the responsible process
questions.answer: Stop and clarify through the responsible process
